name: Pursuer

origin.basis: Maxxis says it began in 1967 as a bicycle-tire maker in Taiwan.

manufacturing.basis: Maxxis' size table does not state where the tire is made.

positioning: Sport-level folding clincher for training miles and casual group rides.

sizes.note: Maxxis lists ETRTO 28-622 and 130 psi for this SKU

weight_basis: Maxxis claims for the black foldable SKUs.

availability.note: Listed on Maxxis' US site with a dealer locator; other regions not verified in this pass.

caveats: The 30C row's ETRTO and pressure look inconsistent in Maxxis' table; check the printed tire.

image.shown: Maxxis render of the Pursuer on its US product page.
image.alt: Maxxis Pursuer road tire render with sidewall logo

rights.usage_note: The maker's own product photo, shown from the maker's website; no copy is stored or redistributed by this project, and no license is asserted.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Checked on 2026-11-03: keyed Xiaohongshu evidence from bounded searches (the first 16-20 result cards of each query, opened exact posts and their visible comments; not exhaustive), coded owner by owner, plus the Sigma Sports and bike-components review lists and every Bicycle Rolling Resistance reader comment on this tire's test pages. Counted only owners who describe their own riding of this exact model and, where it is sold in more than one construction or generation, say which; seller and shop posts, questions, unmounted impressions and reports about other models were left out.

reports.summary: The bike's stock tire for 1,500 km; the Grand Prix 4-Season fitted afterwards felt clearly faster and easier.

checks.note: One owner post; a sale listing is not counted
Only wired versions are listed, with no written review
